transcript: Just in time for Halloween comes a new horror play, 2:22 A Ghost Story. Now I say “new,” but this play has actually existed since 2021. And despite premiering only 5 years ago, it has been remounted 7 times in the U K Alone. plus productions in L A. And Melbourne. And now it is finally in New York. this time starring Jasmine Cephas Jones, Anna Camp, Finn Jones and Martin Marquez. And the show follows a very simple premise. A woman is convinced that her house is haunted after hearing mysterious footsteps several nights in a row at exactly 2:22 am. And so she, along with two friends and her husband, wait up until 2:22 am to get to the bottom of exactly what is happening in the house. Along the way having several philosophical questions around the nature of ghosts and death. Do ghosts actually exist? And if they do, how do they materialize in our world? And how do you square that against logic and known science? And of course, this is a ghost story, so it is going to have some scares, most of which are just loud noises that make you jump. But otherwise I did not find this play to be very scary. It's much more creepy and Philosophical, with most of the actual ghost activity happening off stage. It also has a wild ending where we finally learn the nature of what is going on in the house. And I think that's really what's going to make or break this play for a lot of people. And this is definitely one that you are gonna Wanna go into as blindly as possible. Please do not let anyone spoil this play for you, You are just gonna have to see it for yourself.
classificationReason: Creator reviews the Off-Broadway production of 2:22 A Ghost Story, sharing first-hand opinions: 'I did not find this play to be very scary. It's much more creepy and philosophical.' Clearly a personal attendance review.
